newsitem.title: USA: Seagram sells big piece of Time Warner for $1.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: Seagram sells big piece of Time Warner for $1.4 billion.

text.p: Canadian beverage and entertainment giant Seagram Co. Ltd. Wednesday sold nearly half its stake in Time Warner Inc. for $1.39 billion in cash.

Montreal-based Seagram said it sold 30 million shares to brokerage Merrill Lynch & Co. and continues to hold about 26.8 million Time Warner shares. The company said in a statement that it agreed not to sell the rest of the shares for 120 days without Merrill Lynch's consent.
Seagram, the third largest shareholder in Time Warner, has long been considering a sale of its Time Warner holdings.
In March, Seagram Chairman Edgar Bronfman Sr. said he was disappointed that Time Warner stock had not moved the way Seagram expected and he said Time Warner should take steps to reduce its debt load.
Seagram said net proceeds after tax will be about $1.33 billion and will be used to repay debt and buy stock under Seagram's share repurchase programme.

Separately, the company said its board of directors authorised an increase in the size of its repurchase programme to 10 percent of its stock, or up to 23.6 million common shares, subject to making the required filings.
"As we have said before, since our acquisition of Universal Studios Inc. in June 1995, our position in Time Warner has been non-strategic," Seagram President Edgar Bronfman Jr. said in a statement.

"Given the recent price improvement in Time Warner stock, we believe this was an appropriate time to reduce the size of our holdings. We remain a significant shareholder and see prospects for further appreciation in the price of Time Warner stock."
A Time Warner spokesman said the company was not surprised by the decision and was sure Time Warner's new shareholders will "enjoy appreciation in our stock over time."

Seagram acquired 80 percent of Universal in 1995 from Japanese electronics giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. for $5.7 billion in cash. To finance the deal, Seagram sold its 25 percent stake in chemical giant DuPont Inc., fuelling speculation that the company would soon sell its 9.8 percent stake in Time Warner in order to finance its expansion into entertainment.

Universal Studios Inc. operates music, television, film and theme parks. Seagram also owns a fruit juice and spirits business that includes brands such as Chivas Regal, Seagram's V.O. and Tropicana Orange juice.
